newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slightly lower but thin, no big moves se.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slightly lower but thin, no big moves se.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were trading slightly lower on Friday afternoon but volume was thin and big price moves were not expected.
"We don't see anything much happening later. There's no fresh news out there and most people have cleared up their positions and there's no arb business," said a broker.
January Brent was down nine cents at $22.51 a barrel at 1356 GMT just a couple of cents above the day's low of $22.49 which was hit at midday.
The NYMEX is shut on Friday due to the thanksgiving holiday and the IPE is closing early at 1730 GMT.
The volume traded on Brent by 1357 GMT was 7,365 lots compared to a daily average of 40,500 so far this month.
The spot market for prompt Brent cargoes was little changed talking some 35 cents above January and dealers said no deals had been heard.
The oil market barely flinched after OPEC agreed to freeze output on Thursday and Iraq prepared to resume selling its oil for the first time in six years.
"The market looks tight for the first quarter next year irrespective of what OPEc or Iraq do," said a trader.
Some dealers believe weather conditions in Europe and the United States will be pivotal to the next price move.

Independent forecaster, Weather Services Corp (WSC) said on Friday a cold November had resulted in a higher than normal heating demand in the northeast United States but added milder temperatures were seen for the start of December.
December gas oil was unchanged at $217.50 a tonne at 1407 GMT near the middle of a tight $216.50 to $218.00 trading range.
The physical Rotterdam barge market was very quiet with no change to premiums of $2.00 a tonne above the IPE for prompt.
